NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
1649-1659 WEST WOLFRAM ST., CHICAGO

The subject property is currently a vacant parcel, located in an RS3 Residential Single-Unit
(Detached House) District. The Applicants intend to subdivide this vacant parcel into three new
zoning lots: one 40’ lot (1659 W. Wolfram), one 50’ lot (1657 W. Wolfram) and one 40.30” lot
(1655 W. Wolfram). Each new zoning lot will be redeveloped with a new single-family house,
per plans attached. A zoning change is required to amend the existing RS3 district to a revised
RS3 district, in order to substitute Type 1 Plans and Narrative, which were previously approved
for this property under Application Number 20660T1 (prior Zoning Change Ordinance approved
by City Council on 6/25/2021).

(3) from Section 17-2-0306-B Rear Setbacks, which states that in all R districts, the

(b) 1657 W. Wolfram - to reduce the rear setback from 35” required to 2’ proposed

(B) The Applicants also seek relief for administrative adjustment under Section 17-13-1003-K

Rear Yard Open Space:

(1) From Section 17-2-0307 Rear Yard Open Space, which states that an RS3 district is
subject to the minimum rear yard open space standards (225 square feet per dwelling
unit or 6.5% of lot area, whichever is greater, with minimum 15’ diameter of a circle
which must fit within Rear Yard Open Space), and which allows relocation of the
required open space to the roof of an accessory building (Section 17-2-0307-A):

(a) 1659 W. Wolfram - to relocate the minimum of 322 SF of the required open space
to the garage roof top deck.

(b) 1657 W. Wolfram - to relocate the minimum of 402 SF of the required open space
to the garage roof top deck.

(C) The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the
‘PP iB
proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of the above listed optional relief, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
create practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject property has a
substandard depth. The property has been vacant for many years and needs this relief to stimulate
its redevelopment.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible with

the existing land use pattern on the subject block, which is improved with two-story single-family -
houses with similar bulk measurements. Furthermore, the new dwelling units will increase the
variety of available housing stock, in response to the growing housing demand in the
neighborhood.
